body.statement: For every fixed permitted \(c\), the estimator \(\delta_n^\star\) is total and there is a finite \(B_c\) such that \[\max_y\mathbb E[(\delta_n^\star-\tau_c(y))^2]\le\frac1n-\Lambda_cn^{-4/3}+B_cn^{-3/2}.\] In addition, the minimax risk under the fixed independent design has the sharp expansion \[R_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(c)=\frac1n-\Lambda_cn^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}).\]
body.justification: It converts the dual score and Airy feedback into a full-label finite-data procedure and fixes the restricted benchmark sharply.
body.gap: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen prove this shape only for two arms; Hull's Theorem 1 has the same two-arm restriction and no multiarm second-order coefficient.
body.consumer: A trialist can implement this prespecified procedure as a restricted benchmark without treating it as a claim about unrestricted design optimality.

obligation.what_is_open: The all-estimator Bayes converse under the fixed independent allocation needed to prove the sharp expansion for \(R_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(c)\).
obligation.obstruction: The frozen primitives contain no prior or information inequality giving the reverse second-order inequality. The uniform risk calculation for \(\delta_n^\star\) is one-sided and cannot imply a minimax lower bound. Full assignment labels remain observable, so a scalar statistic cannot be declared sufficient.
obligation.attempted: The finite-alphabet dual identities and the Airy Taylor expansion were checked directly, yielding the uniform attaining theorem. The scalar-path prior suggested by the presolve was stress-tested, but its likelihood reduction and target-specific Bayes identity are not established for arbitrary labeled estimators.
obligation.partial_result:
The proved uniform-risk upper theorem establishes the total finite-data procedure, the uniform remainder, and both lower-limit inequalities.  What remains is the reverse inequality
\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty}n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-R_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(c)\}\le\Lambda_c,
\]
uniformly against all labeled estimators under the fixed independent design.
